- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next period.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.50), model often underestimates; adjust upward by 2–5% to counteract pessimism.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model frequently overshoots; apply a “cool-down” correction: subtract 3–8% from forecast 2–3 periods ahead.  
- If model forecast is consistently above true outcome over 3+ consecutive days, apply mean reversion: subtract 1–3% per day until convergence with recent 7-day average.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often overreacts to short-term sentiment shifts; use sentiment-weighted smoothing: average 3–5 recent sentiment values to dampen volatility bias.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles (e.g., +1, -1, +1), model may misalign with trend; align forecast to sentiment cycle midpoint (e.g., if 3 bullish then 2 bearish, forecast toward bearish mean).
